questions.problem: Which of the following is the indicator function ${1}_{A}(x)$ of the subset $A={2,4,8}$ of $X={0,2,4,6,8}.$
questions.worked_solution:
An indicator function maps elements from a set to the values $0$ or $1,$ depending on whether the element belongs to a specified subset. The indicator function is designed to "indicate" whether an element is a member of a subset.

More specifically, consider a universal set $X.$ Then, the indicator function of a set $A⊆X$ is the function

$$
{1}_{A}(x)={\begin{aligned}1, & \text{if }x\in A, \\ 0, & \text{if }x\notin A.\end{aligned}
$$

The indicator function of the set ${2,4,8}$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114807/assets/850019897d92b0a8d3340c091cee15342be20e99e7578a9fca23f88804e3bf28.png)

 

Notice that the elements $2,4$ and $8$ (the elements of our subset) are mapped to $1,$ and all other elements are mapped to $0.$

questions.problem:
$$
{1}_{A}(5)=1,\,{1}_{B}(5)=0
$$

Given the values of the indicator functions of the sets $A$ and $B,$ which of the following statements are true?

I. ${1}_{A\,\cap \,B}\,(5)=1$

II. ${1}_{A\,\cap \,B}\,(5)=0$

III. $5\in A\cap B$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the indicator functions of $\overset{―}{A},$ $A\cap B,$ and $A\cup B$ have the following properties:

$$
\begin{aligned}{1}_{\overset{―}{A}}\,(x) & =1-{1}_{A}(x) \\ {1}_{A\,\cap \,B}\,(x) & =min{{1}_{A}(x),{1}_{B}(x)} \\ {1}_{A\,\cup \,B}\,(x) & =max{{1}_{A}(x),{1}_{B}(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is false while statement II is true. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{1}_{A\,\cap \,B}\,(5) & =min{{1}_{A}(5),{1}_{B}(5)} \\  & =min{1,0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is false. Since ${1}_{A\,\cap \,B}\,(5)=0,$ we conclude that $5$ does not belong to $A\cap B.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

canonical_examples.problem:
$$
\mathbf{1}_{A}(-1) = 0, \qquad \mathbf{1}_{B}(-1) = 1
$$

Given the values of the indicator functions of the sets $A$ and $B,$ which of the following statements are true?

I. $\mathbf{1}_{A \,\cup\, B}\,(-1) = 1$

II. $\mathbf{1}_{A \,\cup\, B}\,(-1) = 0$

III. $-1 \in A \cup B$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Recall that the indicator functions of $\overline{A},$ $A \cap B,$ and $A \cup B$ have the following properties:

$$
\begin{aligned}{1}_{\overset{―}{A}}\,(x) & =1-{1}_{A}(x) \\ {1}_{A\,\cap \,B}\,(x) & =min{{1}_{A}(x),{1}_{B}(x)} \\ {1}_{A\,\cup \,B}\,(x) & =max{{1}_{A}(x),{1}_{B}(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true while statement II is false. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{1}_{A\,\cup \,B}\,(-1) & =max{{1}_{A}(-1),{1}_{B}(-1)} \\  & =max{0,1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is true. Since $\mathbf{1}_{A \,\cup\, B}\,(-1) = 1,$ we conclude that $-1$ belongs to $A \cup B.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

Similarly, the indicator functions of $A \cap B$ and union $A \cup B$ can be expressed through the indicator functions of $A$ and $B.$

$$

- For the indicator function of the *union*, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{1}_{A\,\cup \,B}\,(x) & =max{{1}_{A}(x),{1}_{B}(x)} \\  & ={1}_{A}(x)+{1}_{B}(x)-{1}_{A}(x)\cdot {1}_{B}(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We can prove these results by splitting them into cases.

tutorials.title: Properties of Indicator Functions
tutorials.content:
Recall that the indicator function of a set $A \subseteq X$ is the function

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114807/assets/7408ad6ce2700ac59d8e6a78c511ba2b51551e6b9d039ee7e2f8548f4177802e.svg)

Therefore, the indicator function of the complement $\overline{A}$ is given by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14114807/assets/de1a51c00e16d836fde350e0936fb9cb63124c72b49174210be3e6f6faa152da.svg)

This means that the indicator function of $A$ and its complement are related as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{1}_{\overset{―}{A}}\,(x) & =1-{1}_{A}(x)\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, the indicator functions of $A \cap B$ and union $A \cup B$ can be expressed through the indicator functions of $A$ and $B.$

- For the indicator function of the *intersection*, we have: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{1}_{A\,\cap \,B}\,(x) & =min{{1}_{A}(x),{1}_{B}(x)} \\  & ={1}_{A}(x)\cdot {1}_{B}(x)\end{aligned}
$$

- For the indicator function of the *union*, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{1}_{A\,\cup \,B}\,(x) & =max{{1}_{A}(x),{1}_{B}(x)} \\  & ={1}_{A}(x)+{1}_{B}(x)-{1}_{A}(x)\cdot {1}_{B}(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We can prove these results by splitting them into cases.
